label: Born in Beaufort West
description: Born in the small country town of Beaufort West in South Africa.

sources.quote: Born on November 8, 1922, in the small country town of Beaufort West in South Africa, Christiaan Neethling Barnard was one of 4 sons of a church pastor who ministered to the poor.

label: Graduated as a doctor
description: Graduated as a doctor from University of Cape Town Medical School.

sources.quote: but he worked hard and graduated as a doctor in 1946.

label: Received scholarship to University of Minnesota
description: Received a scholarship to the University of Minnesota Medical School.

sources.quote: In 1956, he received a scholarship to the University of Minnesota Medical School, where he soon was drawn to the emerging field of open heart surgery.

label: Returned to Cape Town
description: Returned to Cape Town as a specialist in cardiothoracic surgery and director of surgical research.

sources.quote: In 1958, Barnard returned to Cape Town as a specialist in cardiothoracic surgery and director of surgical research.
He was promoted to associate professor in 1962 and to professor of surgical science in 1972.

label: Performed first human-to-human heart transplant
description: Led the surgical team that performed the first human-to-human heart transplant on Louis Washkansky.

sources.quote: On December 3, 1967, Chris Barnard led the surgical team that performed the first human-to-human heart transplant.

label: Promoted to professor of surgical science
description: Promoted to professor of surgical science.

sources.quote: He was promoted to associate professor in 1962 and to professor of surgical science in 1972.

label: Published autobiography One Life
description: Autobiography One Life, ghostwritten by an experienced professional writer, was a major publishing success worldwide.

sources.quote: In 1970, Barnard's autobiography One Life, ghostwritten by an experienced professional writer, was a major publishing success worldwide.

label: Developed heterotopic heart transplantation technique
description: Barnard and Jacques Losman developed the technique of auxiliary (heterotopic) heart transplantation.

sources.quote: In 1974, Barnard and his junior colleague, Jacques Losman, developed the technique of auxiliary (heterotopic) heart transplantation, in which the donor heart is placed in the chest alongside the patient's own heart.

label: Transplanted xenograft auxiliary hearts
description: Transplanted a xenograft auxiliary heart from a chimpanzee and baboon on two occasions.

sources.quote: On 2 occasions in 1977, when a patient's left ventricle failed acutely after conventional open heart surgery, Barnard transplanted a xenograft auxiliary heart (obtained from a chimpanzee and baboon, respectively) with the hope that it would support the patient until the native heart could recover.
In 1983, at age 61, he took early retirement.
With the sudden death of Christiaan Barnard in Cyprus on September 2, 2001, the world lost not only a pioneering cardiac surgeon but also a charismatic, if controversial, figure.
